newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEICESTER THE LATEST TO MAKE MIDDLESBROUGH SUFFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEICESTER THE LATEST TO MAKE MIDDLESBROUGH SUFFER.

text.p: Erratic Leicester City scored a resounding 2-0 victory against Middlesbrough at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday, stretching the big-spending north-east club's run without a league win to 10 matches.
Leicester's goals came either side of half-time with Steve Claridge putting them ahead in the 45th minute and Muzzey Izzet adding the second a minute after the break.

With Brazilian Emerson absent and apparantly back in South America even though he was eligible to play after completing a three match suspension, and fellow Brazilian Juninho on the sidelines injured, Middlesbrough were unable to penetrate City's defence, who had conceded five in their last two league games to Everton and Manchester United.
Claridge headed Leicester ahead when, unmarked he headed home a cross from Neil Lennon from six yards out. Middlesbrough's woes continued when Izzet scored from 25 yards out.

After a bright start to the season when they won three and drew two of their opening six matches, Middlesbrough have not picked up maximum points in the league since beating Everton on September 14 and are now dangerously close to the relegation zone.
Leicester, promoted last season, moved up moved up from 15th to 12th.
